title: The post-acute effects of COVID-19 are not associated with robust long-term regional or global brain volumetric changes: A Bayesian meta-analytic evidence
title_zh: COVID-19后期影响未与显著的长期局部或全脑体积变化相关：贝叶斯荟萃分析证据
abstract: Acute respiratory and systemic manifestations associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection have been extensively investigated, including their potential effects on brain structure. However, whether structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies converge towards reproducible long-term neuroanatomical alterations following COVID-19 remains unclear, mostly due to high variability in methods and reported results across neuroimaging investigations. The present study applied a Bayesian meta-analytic approach to quantify the strength of the evidence supporting the presence or absence of reproducible brain volumetric alterations following COVID-19 infection. The systematic literature search identified nine independent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) experiments reporting whole-brain volumetric measures and 12 MRI experiments reporting regional volumetric measures (i.e., for specific regions of interest), including a total of 1107 subjects with a history of COVID-19 disease and 609 control participants. The results reported in the selected studies were quantitatively synthesized using the Rouder-Morey common-effect Bayesian meta-analytic framework. Bayes' Factors (BF) were computed to quantify how strongly the available evidence supported the alternative hypothesis of volumetric differences relative to the null hypothesis of no differences. Global analyses provided limited evidence of volumetric differences, with BF₁₀ = 3.286 for whole-brain volume and BF₁₀ = 1.206 for total gray matter volume, corresponding to moderate and anecdotal evidence in favor of the alternative hypothesis, respectively. Regional analyses did not identify reproducible volumetric alterations in any of the 26 examined regions of interest. Overall, the present findings indicate that although several studies reported brain abnormalities detectable by MRI following COVID-19, the available volumetric evidence does not support a consistent pattern.
abstract_zh: 急性呼吸和全身表现与SARS-CoV-2感染相关的研究已被广泛开展，包括其对脑结构的潜在影响。然而，结构磁共振成像（MRI）研究是否在COVID-19后产生可重复的长期神经解剖改变仍不清楚，主要由于神经影像学研究方法和报告结果的高度变异。本文采用贝叶斯荟萃分析方法量化支持或否定COVID-19感染后可重复脑体积改变的证据强度。系统文献检索识别出9项独立的MRI实验报告全脑体积测量，12项MRI实验报告局部体积测量（即特定感兴趣区域），共计1107名COVID-19病史受试者和609名对照参与者。所选研究中的结果使用Rouder-Morey共同效应贝叶斯荟萃分析框架定量合成。计算贝叶斯因子（BF）以量化可用证据支持体积差异的备择假设相对于无差异的零假设的强度。全脑分析显示全脑体积BF₁₀=3.286，灰质总量BF₁₀=1.206，分别对应中等和轻微的证据支持备择假设。局部分析未在26个检查的感兴趣区域中识别出可重复的体积改变。总体而言，本文发现虽然多项研究报告COVID-19后可通过MRI检测到的脑异常，但可用的体积证据并不支持一致的模式。
